findings.reason: the followup is the plan's dispatch surface; left as written it queues done sections and never queues 43 to 46, so the new work is silently excluded from the chain.
findings.text: the open followup f-dwl-s38 states "Sections 38 to 42 are the next work" and its title counts five defects, but plan-section-declarations records s39, s40 and s42 as done and s43, s44, s45 and s46 as implementable, and no followup names 43 to 46, so the followup a coordinator dispatches from names already-done work and omits the four genuinely open sections

findings.reason: the done-when's code-review arm parses the hint the obligation actually prints, so the node discovers the real rubric value and the endpoint still lands; the misnamed values mislead the Why but not the gate.
findings.text: s46's Why says "Obligation hints print `crew dispose … --rubric run` and `--rubric code`", but the dispose argument parser accepts only `figure` or no rubric (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1220-1224) and no obligation producer passes "run" or "code" — a code review's stored record carries the health rubric (reckon/crew/review.py:2231), so the hint that is refused prints `--rubric health`, not the values the section names

response_events.note: the followup naming sections 38 to 42 is resolved with its outcome and a new one names sections 43 to 46

wiring-1.note: the followup naming sections 38 to 42 is resolved with its outcome and a new one names sections 43 to 46

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §35 resolves and states the conflict-repair guard s43 builds on; in imas-efit acfc1d2c2 is on origin/develop and ff00628ff is its child and is not on the primary branch, matching s43's "manifest commit is not on the primary branch".
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of s43, s44, s45 and s46 names a test file with per-case arms and a declared negative control that can fail (a repair resume launched, no such command, the partition absent, the rubric refused).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each section's arm logs sit under the run directory, a durable path that survives the run, each carrying its revision, literal command and closing EXIT= line.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the four sections and their test files are named by the mechanism (no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags), and no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s46's Why names `--rubric run` and `--rubric code`, but no producer in the tree prints either value: the dispose verb accepts only `figure` or no rubric and a code review's record carries the health rubric, so the value actually emitted is not the one the section names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of the four changed sections carries one deliverable that one verdict closes.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the open followup f-dwl-s38 names sections 38 to 42 as the next work while the section declarations record s39, s40 and s42 as done and s43 to s46 as implementable but unnamed, so the chain a coordinator dispatches from excludes the four new sections.
